correctness.rationale: Necessity follows by the indegree sum and existence of a source. In the induction, deleting a zero-bit vertex as source toggles the opposite part, preserving feasibility because the edge count drops by the size of that part. For parts of size at least two, if deleting a zero on side A makes every remaining bit one, then A had only that zero and B was all zero. Deleting a zero on B instead turns all the originally odd A bits to zero and avoids the obstruction. If A was all one, deleting a zero from B also works. Stars are forced by the leaf bits and the global sum. The all-odd vector is globally feasible only for two even part sizes. For K(2,b), every simple directed cycle is a 4-cycle and exists precisely when both mixed columns occur. Thus odd columns use one common type, and the number of all-one columns fixes the row bits modulo two. If there are even columns, flipping one fixed even column pairs the assignments of the two row parities. This gives 2^(b−1) at t=0 and 2^(b−t) when 0<t<b. At t=b, the two mixed choices give the two distinct feasible row signatures if b is odd, or both give (0,0) if b is even. An independently written literal orientation census using Kahn sorting passed 1,580 signature checks (790 globally feasible) and 504 two-row fibre checks; scope was 1≤a≤3, a≤b≤5, plus K(2,6) and K(2,7). evidence: In the Walsh source's encoding a zero third-row bit makes that row a source when fixed in every column. Restrict the column sets to integers 0,1,2,3 by averaging over the third-row frequency in each column. In the positive sum over row orders the surviving sets are {0} twice, {0,1} and {0,2} once each, and {0,1,3}, {0,2,3} once each. The subtracted terms restrict to {0,1}, {0,2}, {0,3}, and {0} three times, with the last positive term contributing {0}. Cancellation leaves the two products for {0,1,3} and {0,2,3}, minus the product for {0,3}. Inverting therefore counts two independent-column families with common mixed type, subtracting the all-unmixed overlap.

Prescribed column parity with t>0 eliminates the overlap; each family has 2^(b−t−1) assignments when an even column is available, with row parity deciding which families contribute when none is available. At t=0 the two terms and overlap all have 2^(b−1) assignments. In the Walsh encoding row sums are indegrees and the column indegree is 2 minus its column sum, which gives the same parity constraints and the same boundary values.
